title: Brain areas in memory
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:42Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers immune memory cells in biology, while the new point teaches the brain structures involved in explicit and implicit memory, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Brain areas in memory
card: helps form new explicit memories, such as facts and events. It does not hold them for good.
the outer layer of the brain, where explicit memories are stored over the long term.
adds emotion to memories. Emotional events are often remembered more strongly.
the basal ganglia help with learned skills and habits, and the cerebellum helps with conditioned responses and coordinated movement.
draft.remember: Hippocampus forms, neocortex stores, amygdala adds emotion, basal ganglia and cerebellum run implicit memory.

a.q: Which brain area is mainly involved in forming new explicit memories?
a.why: The hippocampus helps form new memories of facts and events. The amygdala is the tempting option, but it adds emotion to memories rather than forming them.
a.clue: Think of the area that forms memories, not one that adds feeling.

b.q: After a car braked suddenly nearby, Leila vividly remembers the event and still feels afraid. Which area best explains the strong emotion in the memory?
b.why: The amygdala adds emotion to memories, which is why the fear remains. The hippocampus helps form the memory of the event, but it is not the area that adds the feeling.
b.clue: Which area adds feeling to a memory?

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the VCE roles of the hippocampus, neocortex, amygdala, basal ganglia and cerebellum, and both questions have one clear answer with explanations that agree with the card.
